excerpt: Robust Intelligence built a platform to test and protect AI models from threats such as prompt injection and data poisoning. Cisco completed its acquisition in September 2024.
content:
Robust Intelligence was an AI security company. Its platform tested machine learning and generative AI models before deployment and then checked the inputs and outputs of AI applications in production, to catch problems such as prompt injection, jailbreaking and data poisoning. SiliconANGLE described it as protecting AI models and the data they use across the whole development-to-production lifecycle, with automated model assessment and risk mitigation. Its GitHub profile summed up the mission as secure deployment of artificial intelligence. Yaron Singer and Kojin Oshiba co-founded the company, according to FinTech Global.

Acquisition by Cisco

On 26 August 2024 Cisco announced that it intended to acquire Robust Intelligence. In a Cisco blog post, Tom Gillis, who led Cisco's security business, said the deal would help Cisco protect customers' AI applications against emerging threats, and on 24 September 2024 Cisco updated the post to say the acquisition was complete. The price was not disclosed. FinTech Global reported that Robust Intelligence had raised $44 million and had been valued at over $200 million before the deal; Cisco had also invested through Cisco Investments, SiliconANGLE noted. Robust Intelligence's technology now sits within Cisco's security products, and robustintelligence.com redirects to a Cisco page explaining that Robust Intelligence is part of Cisco, under its AI Defense product.

Pricing

Robust Intelligence is no longer sold as a separate product, and it never published a price list. Cisco sells its AI security capabilities through its own sales channels.

What this means for buyers

Organisations looking for what Robust Intelligence offered, such as AI model validation and an AI firewall for generative AI applications, would now evaluate Cisco AI Defense or independent AI security vendors.

This page is based on Cisco's announcement and on SiliconANGLE and FinTech Global coverage of the deal.
